title: Regime-Locked Measurement as a General Structural Constraint: Cross-Domain Framework, Operational Meta-Regime Protocol, and Quantitative Regime-Appropriateness Scoring
description: Formalizes regime-locked measurement as a general structural constraint and identifies a shared structural pattern across six domains. Introduces a quantitative regime-appropriateness score α(ϕ, R) ∈ [0,1], a blind-set taxonomy (ontological, methodological, instrumental), and a five-step meta-regime protocol with residual-based blind-set inference. A worked example in AI alignment highlights a previously invisible class of change (“convergence drift”), and the paper states explicit falsification criteria and self-applies its constraints.
author: Morten Magnusson

regime_definition.description: Defines a regime as instrument I, validity domain V, blind set B, and gradient sensitivity G.

regime_locked_measurement.latex: m \in V(R_i) \ \text{and} \ m \notin V(R_j), \quad i \neq j
regime_locked_measurement.description: A measurement is regime-locked if it falls within one regime’s validity domain and outside another’s.

alpha_score.description: Quantifies how appropriate regime R_i is for phenomenon \phi; 1 is fully appropriate, 0 is entirely blind.

alpha_selection_rule.description: Selects the regime with maximal appropriateness for a given phenomenon.

cdvc.description: Cross-Disciplinary Vector Convergence: a signal present across at least three independent regimes/domains.

meta_regime_mapping.description: Defines a meta-regime that evaluates the appropriateness score for a regime-phenomenon pair.

residual_definition.description: Residuals as the difference between observed data and the instrument’s model output.

residual_inference_rule.description: Structured residuals are treated as candidates for blind-set inference, subject to cross-regime testing.

key_results.main_finding: Defines regime-locked measurement and delivers an operational toolkit—α-scoring, blind-set taxonomy, and a meta-regime protocol—that surfaces blind spots (e.g., convergence drift in AI alignment) otherwise invisible within fixed regimes.

sealed_predictions.statement: If residuals exhibit systematic structure (clustering, scale-dependence, or external correlation), then cross-regime remeasurement or model-switching will recover part of that structure and increase \alpha(\phi, R) relative to the original regime.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Prospective tests where structured residuals are observed and multiple independently designed alternative regimes are applied, yet none increase \alpha or recover the residual structure.

sealed_predictions.statement: Across tasks where ground-truth or strong external validation exists, continuous \alpha-scoring will outperform binary regime selection in regime choice (e.g., predictive adequacy or out-of-sample performance).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Prospective multi-domain evaluations showing no statistically significant improvement of \alpha-based selection over a binary baseline (e.g., Bayes-factor thresholding).

sealed_predictions.statement: A meta-regime protocol targeting AI alignment evaluations can detect convergence drift that deviation-focused instruments systematically miss.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Operational deployment where cases flagged as convergence drift fail independent verification while existing deviation-focused tools identify equal or more such cases without higher false positives.

kill_criteria: KC1: Demonstrate a reliable within-regime method (no change to instrument class or assumptions, i.e., fixed I and V) that detects phenomena previously classified as belonging to the blind set B; this contradicts the regime-locked unmeasurability claim.

KC2: In prospective, pre-registered evaluations across at least three independent domains, \alpha(\phi, R) fails to improve regime selection relative to a binary baseline (e.g., Bayes factors) on predictive adequacy or recovery of held-out structure.

KC3: Show that purported CDVC instances in the surveyed domains arise from cross-domain borrowing or shared bias and lack independent predictive content, eliminating CDVC as a useful indicator within this framework.

KC4: Provide counterexamples where absence of signal within a regime is reliably distinguishable from absence of phenomenon without altering regime parameters (I, V, B, G), thereby invalidating the key property that absence of signal is observationally indistinguishable from absence of phenomenon.

KC5: For the AI alignment case, show that convergence drift is fully detectable by existing deviation-focused instruments when properly configured, and the meta-regime protocol adds no unique detections or increases false positives.
subtitle: Cross-Domain Framework, Operational Meta-Regime Protocol, and Quantitative Regime-Appropriateness Scoring
abstract: Formalises regime-locked measurement as a general structural constraint. Shared structural pattern across six domains. Three contributions: alpha-score alpha(phi, R) in [0,1], blind-set taxonomy (ontological/methodological/instrumental), and five-step meta-regime protocol. Worked example identifies convergence drift in AI alignment.

regime.B: Blind set (typically invisible from within R)
regime.key_property: Absence of signal is indistinguishable from absence of phenomenon

regime_locked_measurement.definition: m in V(R_i) and m not in V(R_j) for i != j
regime_locked_measurement.meaning: Phenomena in B(R_i) are not merely unmeasured — they are unmeasurable within R_i

cdvc.definition: sigma in intersection V(R_k) for N >= 3 domains

residual_inference.procedure: r = data - model(I); test for clustering, scale-dependence, correlation

s0_s1_conjecture.description: At gradient extremes, different generative processes produce indistinguishable outputs
s0_s1_conjecture.ai_formulation: Deep framework integration (S0) vs superficial linguistic mirroring (S1)
s0_s1_conjecture.connection: Identifiability problem in inverse problems / latent-variable models

domains.residual_signal: Pre-9/11 cross-agency signals in each B
2008 crisis: low-volatility calibration blind at boundary

protocol.name: Meta-Regime Evaluation Protocol (Algorithm 1)
protocol.input: Instrument I, target phenomenon phi, candidate regimes {R_1,...,R_n}

steps.name: Cross-Regime Check
steps.action: For each b in B_i, test if b in V_j for some j != i

steps.name: Residual Analysis
steps.action: Test residuals for structure -> B_inferred candidates

steps.name: Alpha-Scoring
steps.action: Estimate alpha; flag if below threshold; report B types

worked_example.step1: Current instruments in deviation-detection regime. V: violations. B: convergence drift.
worked_example.step2: B_known includes convergence drift (B_meth). Detection: switch to convergence evaluation.
worked_example.step3: Detectable from interpretability regime (mechanistic probes of internal representations).
worked_example.step4: Persistent high-quality responses reclassified as B_inferred candidates.
worked_example.step5: alpha ~ 0.5-0.7 (heuristic). B_meth indicates closeable by paradigm expansion.

framework_level: Measurement system demonstrated with B = empty (no blind spots across boundaries)
Six-domain convergence shown to arise from shared methodological artefact
protocol_level: Protocol fails to detect planted blind spots in controlled setting
Alpha fails to discriminate between known-different regimes
conjecture_level: General method reliably distinguishes S0/S1 from output alone

limitations: CDVC: indicator, not proof (shared cognitive bias possible)
Provenance: regime concept from thermodynamic cosmology
Evidential asymmetry: some cases well-sourced, others conceptual

implications.scientific_methodology: No single methodology can claim observational completeness
implications.ai_governance: Alignment evaluation should include convergence monitoring alongside deviation monitoring
